title: GPT-4 lists immune-mediated hemolytic anemia among causes of a Border Collie's worsening anemia; a second vet confirms it and treats the dog, which almost fully recovers
summary: ChatGPT Plus running GPT-4 listed immune-mediated hemolytic anemia among causes of a dog's worsening anemia; a second veterinarian confirmed it, and the owner reported an almost full recovery.
account: A Twitter user, Cooper (@peakcooper), had a Border Collie, Sassy, that had been treated for babesiosis but worsened. She had pale gums and more severe anemia. The first vet found no cause and advised waiting. He entered two sets of bloodwork into ChatGPT Plus running GPT-4. It said that it was not a veterinarian, then listed possible underlying causes including immune-mediated hemolytic anemia (IMHA). At a second clinic he asked about IMHA. The vet agreed after further tests, treatment began, and Cooper reported an almost full recovery. He wrote about it on Twitter on 25 March 2023. GPT-4 reached ChatGPT Plus subscribers on 14 March 2023, so the consultation took place between 14 and 25 March 2023. The New York Post, India Today and Business Insider reported the thread (27 to 30 March). Cooper did not respond to Insider, and no veterinarian has spoken publicly.
purpose: GPT-4, served through ChatGPT, is a general-purpose conversational model built to answer questions and follow instructions. Answering a diagnostic question about a dog's bloodwork is an instance of that general use, not a designed veterinary function. The model itself prefaced its answer by saying it is not a veterinarian.
taxonomy_note: The patient is a dog, and the owner's gain is its recovery after a candidate diagnosis the model surfaced.

ratings.reason: By the owner's own account the diagnosis led to treatment and his dog's near-full recovery. The account is self-reported and unverified by any clinician. The beneficiary is one owner and one animal.

ai_role.statement: From the owner's typed description and two sets of blood results, GPT-4 explained the trend in the bloodwork. When asked what else could underlie the anemia, it listed candidate causes including IMHA. The owner chose IMHA to put to a second veterinarian, who confirmed it after further tests and treated the dog. Whether that vet would have reached IMHA unprompted is unknown. The owner himself notes IMHA is a common complication of babesiosis, so the counterfactual is unproven. The owner reported that GPT-3.5 did not reach the diagnosis. He said the tool “should be a tool to be used by professionals”.

fields.summary: ChatGPT Plus running GPT-4 listed immune-mediated hemolytic anemia among causes of a dog's worsening anemia; a second veterinarian confirmed it, and the owner reported an almost full recovery.
fields.account: A Twitter user, Cooper (@peakcooper), had a Border Collie, Sassy, that had been treated for babesiosis but worsened. She had pale gums and more severe anemia. The first vet found no cause and advised waiting. He entered two sets of bloodwork into ChatGPT Plus running GPT-4. It said that it was not a veterinarian, then listed possible underlying causes including immune-mediated hemolytic anemia (IMHA). At a second clinic he asked about IMHA. The vet agreed after further tests, treatment began, and Cooper reported an almost full recovery. He wrote about it on Twitter on 25 March 2023. GPT-4 reached ChatGPT Plus subscribers on 14 March 2023, so the consultation took place between 14 and 25 March 2023. The New York Post, India Today and Business Insider reported the thread (27 to 30 March). Cooper did not respond to Insider, and no veterinarian has spoken publicly.
